 Clockwatch Premier League Manchester United v Bournemouth, Liverpool v Brighton and more: clockwatch – live
 ⚽️ Premier League updates from 2pm GMT
 ⚽️ Live scoreboard | Send Daniel an email Daniel 
 LIVE  Updated  1m ago Daniel Harris Sun 25 Oct 2026 10.36 EDT First published on Sun 25 Oct 2026 08.15 EDT Share Key events 7m ago GOAL! Hull City 1-0 Brentford (McBurnie 24 pen) 
 13m ago GOAL! Liverpool 2-0 Brighton & Hove Albion (Isak 21) 
 17m ago GOAL! Liverpool 1-0 Brighton & Hove Albion (Wirtz 17)

 Diogo Dalot is challenged by Rayan at goalless opening half at Old Trafford. Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters View image in fullscreen Diogo Dalot is challenged by Rayan at goalless opening half at Old Trafford. Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters Daniel Harris Sun 25 Oct 2026 10.36 EDT First published on Sun 25 Oct 2026 08.15 EDT Share Key events 7m ago GOAL! Hull City 1-0 Brentford (McBurnie 24 pen) 
 13m ago GOAL! Liverpool 2-0 Brighton & Hove Albion (Isak 21) 
 17m ago GOAL! Liverpool 1-0 Brighton & Hove Albion (Wirtz 17) 
 1h ago Hull City v Brentford teams 
 1h ago Crystal Palace v Newcastle United teams 
 2h ago Liverrpool v Brighton & Hove Albion teams 
 2h ago Manchester United v AFC Bournemouth teams 
 2h ago Preamble 
 1m ago 10.36 EDT “The Seagulls have been a shambles at the back,” reckons Kári Tulinius. “Being 2-0 down is the least they deserve. Nevertheless, when they mount an attack, Liverpool defend in a panic, and I doubt they’ll keep a clean sheet. There’s no way there won’t be more goals in this match.”
 I ‘m inclined to agree – Brighton attack well and Liverpool defend chaotically. If the former manage a livener before the latter bag a clincher, this could be a really exciting contest.
 Share 2m ago 10.34 EDT United are offering so little in attack – no width, no 1v1 ability, no sharp passing – and when, as I type, a lovely flick behind the standing leg allows Baleba to find Tielemans, Mbeumo checks his run and the attempted through-pass is easily cut out.
 Share 4m ago 10.32 EDT Better from United, Yoro into Tielemans, who flicks superbly for Baleba down the right. He’s got Mbeumo in the middle, but roughly 94 defenders blocking the route to him, and Hill does well to slide in and intercept the cross.
 Share 6m ago 10.30 EDT A decent ball in from Adams, to which an unsighted Evanilson can’t quite introduce a head. Bournemouth haven’t had that many chances, but they’ve had loads of good situations, whereas United have had none.
 Share 7m ago 10.29 EDT GOAL! Hull City 1-0 Brentford (McBurnie 24 pen)
 We’re not shown for what it was given, but McBurnie dispatches it with a confident roll, Kelleher diving out of the road.
 View image in fullscreen Oli McBurnie puts Hull ahead from the spot. Photograph: Anna Gowthorpe/Shutterstock Share Updated at  10.33 EDT 8m ago 10.28 EDT United are just so careless with the ball. Lammens catches a cross and tries to set a counter in motion, but his roll-out sells Mbeumo short and instead, Bournemouth counter. Oh and Andre Santos was booked a few minutes for a lunge; the same has since been done by and to Tyler Adams.
 Share 11m ago 10.26 EDT It didn’t look great initially ad they’re still too easy to get at, but we can now say that Liverpool have made a decent start under Andoni Iraola. They’ve got into the habit of winning, Isak is scoring, and they’ve loads of attacking options, while Araujo has given them physicality and aggression they lacked not just last season but even the one before when they won the league.
 Share 13m ago 10.23 EDT GOAL! Liverpool 2-0 Brighton & Hove Albion (Isak 21)
 It’s taken a while, but Alexander Isak is a Liverpool player now. Boscagli makes a mess controlling an Alisson kick, Barcola does really well to rob him, and from there, it’s simple competence, a careful cross into the middle and a composed sidefooted finish. Yasiin Ayari will be feeling very, very poorly, and this could yet get a lot worse.
 View image in fullscreen Alexander Isak makes it 2-0 to Liverpool. What a start for the home side! Photograph: Jan Kruger/Getty Images Share Updated at  10.26 EDT 16m ago 10.21 EDT Liverpool keep at it, Verbruggen forced to dive full-length to stop a shot directed across him by Gakpo. Meantime, back in Manchester, it’s now a more even game, though Boournemouth know they can pretty much allow Dalot to have the ball in dangerous areas because nothing will happen thereafter – and, as I type, he lashes a hopeful shot miles from anywhere.
 Share 17m ago 10.19 EDT GOAL! Liverpool 1-0 Brighton & Hove Albion (Wirtz 17)
 That is how much Brighton will regret missing that chance. Araujo does brilliantly down the right – what an acquisition he’s been so far – ruckusing hard to recover possession before crossing low. The ball hits Gross, lands in front of Wirtz, and though he shoots seeking the far corner, a huge deflection off Andres wrongfoots Verbruggen and gives Liverpool the lead.
 View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz fires Liverpool in front! Photograph: Jan Kruger/Getty Images Share Updated at  10.22 EDT 20m ago 10.17 EDT Back to OT and it’s slightly better from United, Mbeumo finding space before running into trouble. They are, though, keeping the ball now, with Baleba seemingly settled into the game.
 Share 21m ago 10.16 EDT Oh, but here come Brighton! They fight down the right, Gomez in behind and taking a pass from Gross before cutting back for Ayari, 10 yards out … who panels over the bar! What a chance that was, and how might Brighton rue spurning it?
 Share 23m ago 10.14 EDT At Anfield, Costinha has replaced Kadioglu, who gives Brighton so much attacking impetus. We’ve barely seen them in the Liverpool half yet, but they’ve done well to survive the opening period … as have United, sort of – so far, their performance is such that to say they’ve done anything well feels ridiculous. And, as I type, a flick off Yoro prevents a cross from arriving at Evanilson.
 Share 25m ago 10.12 EDT The corner comes to nowt, but in possession, United’s players are constantly alone and surrounded, with Bouernemouth’s in space. 
 Share 26m ago 10.10 EDT Here come Bournemouth again, a goals surely in the post; they’re finding overloads and space all over the show. Thsi time, the ball is spread wide, Rayan crosses, and Yoro has to slide in to make a fine last-ditch challenge on Evanilson, who would otherwise have tapped home.
 Share 28m ago 10.09 EDT At Anfield, Liverpool have started quickly, taking advantage of Kadioglu, who steps off with back-knack. A cross from the right picks out Isak too, but his first touch is poor and the ball runs away.
 View image in fullscreen Ferdi Kadioglu is tackled by Ryan Gravenberch. Photograph: Peter Byrne/PA Share Updated at  10.11 EDT 29m ago 10.07 EDT Again, Bournemouth come at United, Tielemans robbed, and they’ve cut through so easily, Rayan one on one with Maguire. Kluivert is square, too, but he opts to shoot, Maguire blocking with a long barrier cricket-type stop.
 Share 31m ago 10.06 EDT At Selhurst, Palace generate a scramble in the Newcastle box, bodies in front of the ball doing enough.
 Share 31m ago 10.05 EDT Bourmemouth appeal for a penalty, though, as the bouncing ball clips Dalot … but it’s hip not hand then, when corner comes in, Rayan is up above Baleba, heading wide of the far post. That was a decent chance, but he couldn’t quite get the leverage necessary.
 Share 33m ago 10.04 EDT At OT, the crowd sing for Carrick; it’s Dalot at left-back, Yoro right, and Heaven in the middle, as Bournemouth attack, winning a corner.
 View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick gives instructions to Amad Diallo from the touchline. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA Share Updated at  10.16 EDT 34m ago 10.03 EDT Our various teams take the knee; it’s still Black History Month for a few more days, so why not educate ourselves by clicking here , to check out or dedicated site?
 Share 36m ago 10.00 EDT Full disclosure: I’ve only got three screens, so I’m afraid Hull v Brentford isn’t being watched. But we’ll be keeping an eye on the gaols and key developments.
 Share 38m ago 09.59 EDT “I have five days to write 11,000 words and complete my minor thesis,” laments Chris Paraskevas, “this is supposed to be my ‘break time’ and I’m looking at the Newcastle lineup trying to figure out how many successful passes Joelinton and Nico Gonzalez will manage between each other (I’m predicting: 3 out of 15 before Big Joe gets sent off). What have I done in a previous to deserve this vertical football purgatory?”
 Existed?
 Share Updated at  09.59 EDT 40m ago 09.57 EDT Righto, here come our teams – at Old Trafford, United are led out by Harry Maguire.
 Share 40m ago 09.56 EDT “I agree with you,” says Tim Stappard. “Mike Walker is bonkers. Utd would have been relegated without Bruno. Maybe that’d have been a good thing though.”
 Don’t get me wrong, I see Bruno’s bad points but, as you intimate, just imagine United im the last nearly-seven-years without him.
 Share 43m ago 09.54 EDT “You’ve just done a rundown on the United team,” begins Robert Hisnay . “Isn’t that a sorry starting 11? The question has to be asked: are they relegation contenders? Unlike 2025 when they finished 15 th and the three newly-promoted teams were abysmal, this season only Coventry City look likely for relegation. So, who are the two clubs worse than United? And for now I’ll leave the Manchester City situation off the table as the appeals and proceedings are unknown.”
 As they often have in the Post-Fergie Wilderness Years TM , United actually have the bones of a good team. Lammens is good, Bruno is elite, while Yoro, Baleba, Mainoo and Sesko have elite potential, and Mbeumo and Cunha are good Premier League players.
 Carrick is, of course, partly responsible for his own situation, but he’s also had rotten luck within injuries; if i’m betting, I don’t think he’s in the job much longer, but if he is, it’s because things have got better, and if he isn’t, I’d expect whoever takes over to make things better because it’s not possible to get much less out of this squad and, as Carrick showed last season, it’s definitely possible to extract very much more.
 Share 50m ago 09.47 EDT Email! “You can’t be serious, Daniel,” begins Matt Walker. “I’ve been watching United for 26 years and we’ve never had a more petulant player on the field. I think the veil slipped more than anything ‘broke him’. He’s a bad teammate and never was captain material. He never would’ve been in position to be captain if the club was run even half decently.”
 Bruno has carried United for the best part of a decade; is it even arguable to the contrary? In that time, he’s barely missed a game despite being the busiest player in world football, playing through injuries, setting standards – in training every day, as well on matchday – while cementing himself as perhaps the best creator around. And like Roy Keane, who those on the outside said was a bad captain because they interpreted his communication style in a particular way, the lads he pays with love and respect him.
 Share 55m ago 09.42 EDT So where is that game? I’d expect Brighton to see weakness down Liverpool’s left, where Van Dijk isn’t what he was – expect to see attackers run at and off him – and Kerkez lack discipline and focus, while Barcola is much better going forwards than backwards. I really like Charalampos Kostoulas, and and I’d expect Brighton to play into him with runners going past, but also looking to hit him with crosses and cut-backs.
 Liverpool, I think, will want to get Barcloa running at Kadioglu, with Kerkez backing him up, while Writz floats seeking to prod Isak through to take snap-shots – his accuracy and power is elevated by how quickly he assesses situations and introduces laces to ball. I also wonder if they look to go at Andres, who is good in the tackle but lack a bit of mobility.
 Share 1h ago 09.38 EDT Brighton, as one might expect, are unchanged following last weekend’s 5-0 kicking of Crystal Palace.
 Share 1h ago 09.37 EDT Now to Anfield, where Rio Ngumoha is benched despite an electrifying display against Villarreal on Tuesday night; Victor Munoz is injured, but his right-wing berth goes to Cody Gakpo, with Bradley Barcola, improved in recent games, on the left. Otherwise, Ryan Gravenberch, back from suspension, is in for the injured Dominik Szoboszlai.
 Share 1h ago 09.30 EDT Bournemouth, meanwhile, will know that on one side, United will have a defender playing out of position. I’m sure they’ll hope to double up down whichever side it is, with Evanilson running off Maguire and Tavernier staying pretty wide, looking to put ball into the box, while Rayan and Kluivert look to run af defenders and attack the area from a little deeper.
 Defensively, Adams and Cook will patrol the central area from which United like to create, with Smith, on the right, playing a little deeper than Truffert, on the left.
 Share 1h ago 09.25 EDT So, where is the game? United will look to build through the middle of the pitch, Santos stepping in between the centre-backs to punch passes forward and Baleba looking to carry whenever he can. There’s not much width or height in this side, so the onus will be on Tielemans, Amad and Mount to slip passes in behind the Bournemouth defence for Mbeumo, who’ll attack the space.
 Share 1h ago 09.22 EDT As for Bournemouth, the headline news the return of Kroupi, who’s on the bench. Otherwise, Rose makes one change to the side which beat Sunderland last weekend, Justin Kluivert replacing Ryan Christie.
 Share 1h ago 09.20 EDT Otherwise, Carrick goes for ballast in the midfield, with Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba, which makes sense, but in front of him, there’s a palpable lack of magic. Matheus Cunha, hooked at half-time in Como, drops out, with Amad one of the least dreadful when he came on, coming in on the right. His numbers tell us he’s not the standard required, but he offers good out-of-possession work and gives the team balance, such as it is, the only dribbles in a team severely lacking one v one ability.
 Otherwise, Mason Mount, every manager’s favourite, is relocated to the left, while Bryan Mbeumo continues up front in the absence of Benjamin Sesko – which tells us plenty about what Carrick thinks of Joshua Zirkzee, despite his goal in midweek.
 Share 1h ago 09.16 EDT Taking a closer look at the United team, Leny Yoro is back after his midweek suspension. Before it, he looked, finally, to have established himself in the first XI and, though he’s a centre-back, I expect he’ll play right-back today, with Ayden Heaven, back in after illness, taking the spot in the centre next to Harry Maguire. That’s because he’d never previously played left-back until forced to fill the spot away to Atletico – one of various things that so exercised Martinez. But now that you don’t ask, I’d probably stick him there again, to get Yoro into his position – he’s actually done better on the left of the two than on the right – and so Digo dalot can play on his natural side. We shall see.
 Share 1h ago 09.12 EDT Hull City v Brentford teams
 Hull City (5-4-1): Tzolakis; Coyle, Ajayi, Egan, Herrington, Giles; Belloumi, Iroegbunam, Slater, Stroud; McBurnie. Subs: Phillips, Morita, Thomas, Gelhardt, McNair, Norton-Cuffy, Crooks, Vaz, Cho.
 Brentford 4-2-3-1): Kelleher; Kayode, Van den Berg, Ajer, Hickey; Sangaré, Jensen; Ouattara, Schade, Lewis-Potter; Thiago. Subs: Valdimarsson, Wilson, Anthony, Collins, Damsgaard, Diouf, Nunes, Schuster, Fredrick.
 Share 1h ago 09.09 EDT Marco Rose says the last three games have passed and his team need to prove themselves again. He’s been in the business long enough to know this could be a good moment to play United, but also a bad one if the players want to turn the noise down.
 As a club they need to get used to the new demands of the Europa League so he needs to use his squad, but i’s good to have Junior Kroupi back, as though he’s not yet 100%, he decides game and is good to have in the locker room.
 Old Trafford is a difficult place to play, but Bournemouth are confident and know what do, it’s just about executing now.
 Share 1h ago 09.07 EDT Crystal Palace v Newcastle United teams
 Crystal Palace (3-4-2-1): Benitez; Richards, Disasi, Canvot; Khakaili, Wharton, Kamada, Mitchell; McNeil, Pino; Mateta. Subs: Matthews, Lerma, Mingueza, Hughes, Doucoure, Chilwell, Osorio, Guessand, Nketiah.
 Newcastle United (4-2-3-1): Hornicek; Dedic, Schar, Burn, Hall; Gonzalez, Joelinton; Murphy, Willock, Barnes; Osula. Subs: Pope, Botman, Bamba, Wissa, Thiaw, Steur, Toure, Elanga, Ramsey.
 Share 2h ago 09.04 EDT Liverrpool v Brighton & Hove Albion teams
 Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Gravenberch; Barcola, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak. Subs: Mamardashvili, Gomez, Endo, Chiesa, Tsimikas, Nyoni, McConnell, Koumas, Ngumoha.
 Brighton & Hove Albion (4-2-3-1): Verbruggen; Kadioglu, Vuskovic, Dunk, Boscagli; Andres, Gross; Gomez, Ayari, De Cuyper; Kostoulas. Subs: Steele, Hadjam, Hinshelwood, Rutter, Promise, Osman, Costinha, O’Riley, Yalcouye.
 Share Updated at  09.04 EDT 2h ago 09.03 EDT Carrick tells Sky that you’ve got options when picking a team, it’s always a difficult decision and they had to make one in the best interests of the team. Asked if it’s because of what he said or how he’s playing, he replies with “Pure football.” 
 Lisandro Martinez isn’t ready yet, he continues, Heaven was ill but has played well and United have strong options off the bench.
 He wants United to play with humility and endeavour, Bournemouth are a really good team and United will have to play well to get a result. They want to flip the run and win a game and today is a good day to do that.
 Share 2h ago 08.59 EDT Manchester United v AFC Bournemouth teams
 Manchester United (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Yoro, Maguire, Heaven, Dalot Santos, Baleba; Amad, Tielemans, Mount; Mbeumo. Subs: Darlow, De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui, Bruno Fernandes, T. Fletcher, Cunha, Lacey, Zirkzee.
 AFC Bournemouth (4-2-3-1): Petrovic; Smith, Hill, Silva, Truffert; Adams, Cook; Rayan, Kluivert, Tavernier; Evanislson. Subs: Soler, Brooks, Di Gregorio, Christie, Gannon-Doak, Diakité, Adli, Kroupi, Rodríguez.
 Share 2h ago 08.38 EDT Reports from Old Trafford, broadcast by Sky, advise us that Bruno Fernandes has been dropped by Michael Carrick. 
 We don’t know if it’s for consistent poor form or midweek insubordination – it could be either or both – but either way, it’s a shame it’s come to this. Ultimately, United have broken Bruno, who’s dedicated his career to elevating a club that has consistently let him down, and though he was out of line in what he said after Como, it didn’t come out of nothing, well earned though his omission is.
 Share 2h ago 08.15 EDT Preamble
 An egg walks into a kitchen looking unhappy, so a chef asks what’s up. “It’s the spurtles,” he says. “They beat me.”
 “What about the forks?” ventures the chef; “Yes, they beat me too,” comes back the response, so there’s a pause while the chef considers.
 “Have you thought about hanging out with Manchester United?” he eventually offers. They don’t beat anyone.”
 It’s now almost two months since United won a league game, and that against promoted Ipswich – who now sit five places above them in the table. They did also manage a victory over Sabah, Champions League debutants, but otherwise, their start to the season has been miserable beyond conception, even by their august standards, and is rapidly getting worse. Already, it looks like yet another manager is toast, and this time, perhaps for the first time, there’s no sense of where they could go next.
 Just three weeks ago, a home game against Bournemouth was as close to a gimme as possible – even for them. Since then, though, consecutive home wins over Sturm Graz, Sunderland and Milan with eight goals scored and none conceded have flipped the Cherries’ mood and they arrive at Old Trafford with Marco Rose ensconced and the club on a buzz. They’ll fancy this, and really who wouldn’t?
 If that was the extent of our afternoon, it’d be plenty, but happily for us, it’s not even close. At Anfield, Liverpool – who’ve also won three on the spin in uplifting fashion – entertain Brighton, already three points clear of third with a game in hand. They’ll know a top-five spot is theirs for the taking and the way they’re playing, who knows what else?
 Those two matches will be our focus, but we’ll also be updating from from KC where Hull, who might just be running out of form after a brilliant start, face Brentford while, at Selhurst, Palace meet Newcastle, struggling badly after a promising start under Matthias Jaissle. Or, in other words, this is going to be a lot of fun.
 Kick-offs: 2pm GMT, baby
